This is the insurer's appeal against the award dated 16.12.2015 passed by the 8th Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Raipur (C.G.) in Claim Case No.
16/2013 whereby a compensation of Rs. 37,58,000/- with interest @ 06% per annum has been awarded in favour of the Claimant and order of pay and recover has been passed.

entities.text: 8th Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Raipur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2 The facts, in brief, necessary for disposal of this appeal, are that on 12/11/2009, around 12 noon near Durga Dharmkanta, Ring Road No. 2, Bhanpur, District Raipur, the driver of truck no.
CG-04/J-2851 (offending vehicle) driven by respondent no. 2 at high speed and negligently, struck and crushed the Respondent No.1 motorcycle bearing registration no. CG-10/E-4125.

As a result,
the Respondent No.1, who was driving the motorcycle, sustained grievous injuries.
The treatment was first provided at Mishra Hospital, Timber Market Road, Pandri, and subsequently at Ramakrishna Care Hospital, Pachpedi Naka, Raipur.
A report of the incident was lodged at Police Station Khamtarai, District Raipur.
The claimant/Respondent No.1 preferred a claim application before the Tribunal claiming total compensation of Rs.55,06,280/-.

Learned Tribunal, after considering the evidence and documents available on record, awarded total compensation of Rs.37,58,000/- with interest @ 6% per annum, from the date of application till its realization, in favour of the claimant.

3 While passing the impugned award, the Tribunal held that the offending vehicle was driving by its driver in breach of policy conditions as the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess valid and effective driving license at the time of accident.

But the offending vehicle was duly insured with the insurance company/appellant therefore, the appellant/insurance company held liable to firstly pay the amount of compensation and then recover it from the driver/owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the appeal.

4 It is contended by learned counsel for the appellant/Insurance Company that on the date of accident driver/Respondent No.2 had not possessed the valid and effective driving license to drove the vehicle, therefore, there was clear breach of policy conditions and the insurance company cannot be held liable for payment of compensation.
Thus, the appeal is liable to be allowed and the Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. ... vs Rajesh Kumar Sen on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6949505/

5 Learned Counsel appearing for Respondent No.1/Claimant supported the impugned award and submitted that the award in question is based on the proper appreciation of the oral as well as documentary evidence which does not call for any interference.
6 There is no representation made on behalf of respondents No.2 & 3.
7 Heard learned counsel for the appellant and perused the record.

8 The principles laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Amrit Paul Singh and Another Vs. Tata AIG General Insurance Company Limited and others reported in (2018) 7 SCC 558 ordering the insurance company to pay first and then recover.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering the facts and circumstances of the present case, particularly the fact that at the time of accident the vehicle was duly insured with appellant/insurance company, it is directed that the insurance company shall first pay the amount of compensation awarded to the claimant/respondent No.1 and then recover the same from the driver and/or owner of the offending vehicle.
9 Learned Tribunal, in para-33 of its award, has held that the vehicle, CG-04/J-2851, was insured by the appellant/insurance company (Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Limited).

entities.text: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Limited
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
It is a well-established principle of the Motor Vehicles Act that the owner is liable for the acts of the driver,
and for the owner's liabilities, the Appellant/insurance company will be held responsible.

However,
it has also been proven in this case that respondent no. 2/driver did not possess a valid and effective driving license on the date of the accident, i.e., 12.11.2009.

Since the offending vehicle, truck no.
CG-04/J-2851, was duly insured with the Appellant/insurance company at the time of accident, it is the primary responsibility of the Appellant to pay the compensation amount of 37,58,000 (thirty-seven lakh fifty-eight thousand rupees) to Respondent No.1/Claimant.
Thereafter, if the Appellant/insurance company desires, it can be recovered the same from respondent no. 2/driver and respondent no. 3/owner by an appropriate recovery proceeding.
In considered opinion of this Court the above finding of the learned Tribunal is a correct finding which does not call for any interference.
10 Accordingly, this appeal of the Insurance Company is dismissed.
11 Record of the Claims Tribunal be sent back along with a copy of this order forthwith for information and necessary action, if any.

Sd/-
(Sanjay Kumar Jaiswal) Judge Shubham Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. ... vs Rajesh Kumar Sen
